```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# load data
treatment.groups <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "treatmentGroups.rds"))

filteredCountsMat <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "filteredCountsMat.rds"))
filteredCountsMatUQ <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "filteredCountsMatUQ.rds"))
topTable.dex <- readRDS(file.path(save_dir, "topTable.dex.rds"))
```

## Introduction

This report contains exploratory data analysis results of the 'airways' package RNAseq data (Himes *et al* 2014).

The data consists of `r ncol(raw.counts.matrix)` samples (`r knitr::combine_words(colnames(raw.counts.matrix))`), and `r length(levels(treatment.groups))` treatment groups (`r knitr::combine_words(levels(treatment.groups), before = "'", sep = " / ", and = "")`).

## Methods

### Filtering, tidying and normalising.

The data were filtered to exclude low-expression counts.
Genes were required to have a minimum of `r paste(min.cpm, pluralize("count", min.cpm))` per million in at least `r min.cpm.fraction` percent of samples. 
After filtering there were `r nrow(filteredCountsMat)` genes retained from the initial `r nrow(raw.counts.matrix)` genes.

In the 'Airway' package data genes are referred to by an accession number (in this case Ensembl ID).
To make it easier to interpret the data, the Ensemble IDs were replaced with the corresponding gene symbol, using the biomaRt package.
In cases where matches were not found, the Ensemble IDs were retained.

Finally, an upper-quartile normalise function was applied to correct for any differences in library depth between samples.

### Differential Gene Expression tests

A differential gene expression analysis between treatment groups was carried out using `edgeR` R package (Chen *et al.* 2024).
The raw library counts for each sample were normalised using the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) proposed by Robinson and Oshlack (2010).

After creating test design and contrast objects, count data was transformed using mean-variance modeling at the observational level using the `voom` function from the `limma` R package (Law *et al.* 2016).
A linear model was fit and differential expression statistics were calculated using an empirical Bayes method (`efit` function from `limma` R package).

## Results

### Normalisation

Upper quartile normalisation increased the consistency of counts between samples (compare Figs. 1 and 2).

```{r unnormalised, echo=FALSE}
boxplot(log2(1+filteredCountsMat), las=2, cex.axis=0.5, cex=0.5,
        ylab="log2(1+counts)",
        xlab="Samples")
```

*Figure 1. Box plot of un-normalised counts by sample*

```{r normalised, echo=FALSE}
boxplot(log2(1+filteredCountsMatUQ), las=2, cex.axis=0.5, cex=0.5,
        ylab="log2(1+counts)",
        xlab="Samples")
```

*Figure 2. Box plot of upper-quartile normalised counts by sample*

### Gene of interest

The differences in UQ-normalised mRNA counts between treatment groups for the gene of interest, `r gene.of.interest`, are shown in Fig. 3 below
The difference in counts between treatment groups for this gene was `r if(topTable.dex[which(topTable.dex$ID==gene.of.interest),]$adj.P.Val < 0.05) 'statistically significant' else 'not statistically significant'` (p-value = `r signif(topTable.dex[which(topTable.dex$ID==gene.of.interest),]$adj.P.Val, digits = 2)`).

```{r gene-of-interest, echo=FALSE}
plot(log2(1+filteredCountsMatUQ[gene.of.interest,]), x=treatment.groups,
     ylab="UQ-normalised mRNA counts", xlab="", main=gene.of.interest)
```

<i>Figure 3. Box plot of differences in UQ-normlised mRNA counts between treatment groups for `r gene.of.interest`</i>

### Volcano plot

The volcano plot below (Fig. 4) shows the distribution of statistical significance (adjusted P value) versus magnitude of change (fold change).
The 30 most-significant genes are annotated.
Of the 30 genes with most statistically significant differences, `r table(sign(topTable.dex$logFC[1:30]))['-1']` were downregulated, and `r table(sign(topTable.dex$logFC[1:30]))['1']` were upregulated.

```{r volcano-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.align='left', out.width='100%', fig.cap='Figure 4. Volcano plot with the 30 most-significant genes labelled'}
knitr::include_graphics(paste0('../',save_dir, 'volcano_plot.png'))
```
